stories.new_fact: Reuters reported the Trump-Xi summit left the two-month truce extension as the clearest outcome while tariffs, rare earths, Taiwan and technology restrictions remained unresolved.
stories.new_takeaway: Companies get a longer clock but not a settled operating rulebook for procurement, licenses, inventory and export-control decisions.
stories.why_now: The summit occurred September 24 and the morning-after practical question is what actually changed after the meeting.
stories.previous_coverage: September 24 previewed the summit and truce extension before outcomes were known; today's segment uses the lack of settlement as the new fact and shifts the takeaway to post-meeting operating ambiguity.
stories.uncertainty: Follow-up agency statements or Chinese official releases could add enforceable commitments after cutoff.
stories.watch: Treasury, Commerce or Beijing publication naming goods, chip categories, rare-earth handling, Taiwan language or the January 10 truce date.

stories.new_fact: Columbus file 2560-2026 is listed on the September 28 council agenda and would require Columbus Water and Power to establish peak rates, fees or charges for large-load or high-volume users.
stories.new_takeaway: The local issue is cost causation: whether data centers and other high-volume users pay for peak infrastructure instead of shifting costs to flatter residential and small-commercial demand.
stories.why_now: The agenda is the upcoming Monday action point after the ordinance's first reading; Friday listeners can watch the vote before the weekend passes.
stories.previous_coverage: September 18 covered the guardrail proposal; this is a narrower agenda-trigger update with more detail on demand charges, rate classes and the Home Road capacity issue.
stories.uncertainty: Council approval would direct CWP to produce a proposal; it would not itself set final rates.
stories.watch: September 28 council vote and the rate proposal CWP brings back with tiered charges, demand charges, minimum bills or contracted-capacity assumptions.

stories.new_fact: Fannie Mae says lenders may apply September rental-income changes immediately but must do so no later than November 1, 2026.
stories.new_takeaway: Rental-income qualification becomes an implementation and QC workflow issue: update training, worksheets, bookmarked guide sections and LOS aids before mandatory use.
stories.why_now: The September page and policy communications were updated after the September Selling Guide update, and the mandatory implementation window is active.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent lending segments covered ARM counseling, MBS disclosure and appraisal/document updates; no recent episode led with rental-income review implementation.
stories.uncertainty: The public page summarizes changes; exact file impacts require lenders to compare the Selling Guide text and any investor overlays.
stories.watch: Fannie Mae FAQs, Ask Poli updates, aggregator overlays or investor bulletins before November 1.

stories.new_fact: BNP Paribas and Google Cloud announced a five-year partnership to expand BNP Paribas access to Google Cloud infrastructure, Gemini Enterprise and Gemini models, with initial CIB use cases including LLM@CIB and agentic AI.
stories.new_takeaway: At a large bank, the decision changes platform approval and vendor concentration more than it proves productivity; measured CIB task outcomes are still missing.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent bank AI segments covered Paywhere, Deutsche Bank KYC and Mastercard/Danske payments; this moves to CIB knowledge work and cloud/model platform approval.
stories.uncertainty: No baseline or measured result was disclosed for analyst time saved, errors, compliance review time, trade-support quality or customer outcomes.
stories.watch: Named CIB task volume, human review rate, error rate, production status and whether Gemini changes a bank decision or only drafts work faster.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added BNP Paribas / Google Cloud, CIB generative and agentic AI platform expansion, announced status, company-claim evidence.

stories.new_fact: Prosaic Intelligence published ConfAIde data on privacy-sharing error rates for fourteen API model configurations, including Claude Opus 5.5, GLM 5.3 Flash, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.
stories.new_takeaway: The benchmark is more useful as a privacy-failure test pattern than as a hard model ranking because the score-only feed omits measurement dates, sample sizes and confidence intervals.
stories.why_now: The benchmark page reports data published September 25, 2026.
stories.previous_coverage: September 24 covered OpenAI and Anthropic pricing/access; this uses a fresh safety benchmark and a different takeaway about privacy-sensitive enterprise copilots.
stories.uncertainty: The results are single-turn API configuration tests and do not establish behavior inside consumer apps or enterprise systems with custom prompts, tools and permissions.
stories.watch: Methodology updates, confidence intervals, app-level replications or bank-specific privacy test suites.
stories.frontier_bar: Benchmark or evaluation that changed how models are compared, with safety/privacy evidence.

stories.new_fact: Reuters reported the S&P 500 ended nearly unchanged Thursday, Nasdaq was nearly flat, Dow fell about one-third of a percent, and the 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest since 2004.
stories.new_takeaway: The practical pressure remains long yields and oil, which feed into mortgage rates, municipal borrowing, utility capacity and AI infrastructure finance.
stories.why_now: Thursday's market close is the latest available market context before Friday morning.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent scripts connected markets to rates and AI infrastructure; this is kept compact and not counted toward freshness.
stories.uncertainty: Friday trading and subsequent policy comments can change the market signal quickly.
stories.watch: Oil, long Treasury yields, MBS pricing and any U.S.-China follow-up that affects risk appetite.

stories.new_fact: The Columbus forecast called for a clear morning, sunshine, a high near 71, a mid-40s overnight low and a sunny Saturday near 74.
stories.new_takeaway: Layers early and outdoor windows later are the useful planning moves.
stories.why_now: Weather is current for Friday morning planning.
stories.previous_coverage: September 24 covered a clearer, cool day; this is routine local planning.
stories.uncertainty: Local forecast pages update throughout the morning.
stories.watch: Any change to weekend sunshine or morning lows in later NWS updates.
